page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine offering a balanced ratio of compute to system memory. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz with two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 32 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Cache resources comprise 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB shared L3 cache, complemented by support for AVX-512 and AES instructions. The configuration does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring cloud-attached network storage for filesystem persistence.

Benchmark evaluations reveal solid multi-core execution alongside restrained single-threaded performance. The instance registers a PassMark CPU score of 9929.97 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4895.0, supported by a stress-ng multi-core measurement of 8682.55. Key-value operations demonstrate steady throughput, achieving 10.22 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Conversely, single-threaded metrics fall in the lower quartiles, with Geekbench single-core reaching 907.0, single-threaded gzip compression recording 18.97 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput measured at 5.98 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 61.2 GB/sec while write bandwidth measures 47.14 GB/sec.

Given the balance of dedicated vCPUs and memory capacity, the instance offers practical resource density for mid-tier application hosting. Architectural tradeoffs center on its older Skylake-era baseline, which exhibits lower per-core efficiency compared to newer architectures while maintaining steady parallel throughput across its 8 vCPUs. The ecs.n2.xlarge instance fits multi-threaded general-purpose services, mid-sized caching nodes, backend worker processes, software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice clusters that do not rely on high-frequency single-thread execution.

Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The server includes instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and AES, but includes no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates mid-range multi-core efficiency, logging a Geekbench multi-core score of 4895.0, a PassMark CPU score of 9929.97, and 10.22 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core metrics fall into lower performance tiers. This profile makes ecs.n2.xlarge well-aligned with distributed microservices, standard web application hosting, build systems, and parallel background batch workloads.
